title: Honda Prelude Limited Edition Avrupa pazarına geliyor
summary: Japonya'daki yoğun ilgi üzerine Honda, özel renk ve detaylara sahip Prelude Limited Edition modelini Avrupa'ya getirme kararı aldı.
body:
Honda, Japonya'da yoğun ilgi gören hibrit coupe modeli için hazırladığı **Honda Prelude** Limited Edition versiyonunu Avrupa pazarına sunmaya hazırlanıyor. Motor1'in aktardığına göre, bu özel model Japon pazarındaki başarısının ardından sonbaharda Avrupalı otomobil severlerle buluşacak.

## Tasarım ve donanım detayları

Avrupa'ya gelecek olan yeni model, standart versiyondan farklı olarak Premium Crystal Garnet Metallic adı verilen koyu kırmızı özel bir dış renk seçeneğiyle geliyor. Otomobilin dış görünümü tamponlardaki kırmızı detaylar, 19 inç siyah jantlar ve arkalarında yer alan Brembo fren kaliperleriyle tamamlanıyor. İç mekanda ise Bordeaux adı verilen bordo tema, özel paspaslar, direksiyon, ön konsol ve koltuklardaki kırmızı dikişler ile ön panelde el yapımı izlenimi veren işlenmiş Prelude logosu dikkat çekiyor.

## Performans ve beklentiler

Kaputun altında radikal bir güç artışı sunmayan bu özel sürüm, tasarımı ve iç detaylarıyla öne çıkıyor. Honda, araçta Civic modeline kıyasla adaptif amortisörler, daha geniş iz genişlikleri ve çift pinyonlu elektronik hidrolik direksiyon sistemi gibi Type R modelinden alınan bazı donanımlara yer veriyor. Şirket şu an için daha güçlü bir Type R versiyonu, daha ucuz bir baz donanım veya manuel şanzıman seçeneği sunmayı planlamıyor.

**Neden önemli?** Japonya pazarındaki yüksek talep sonrasında Avrupa'ya taşınan bu özel seri, markanın hibrit coupe modelinin sunduğu kişiselleştirme ve tasarım seçeneklerini genişletiyor.

source_texts.text:
Honda's Limited-Run Prelude Was Such A Hit In Japan, It's Now Coming To Europe
“Overwhelming response” at home has prompted Honda to bring the swanky coupe’s exclusive colorway to other markets.
Honda is happy to report that, seemingly against all odds, customers actually want its new hybrid coupe that brings back an important nameplate. Well, at least if we’re strictly talking about the Limited Edition it introduced earlier this year in Japan. The special Prelude has received an “overwhelming response” in its domestic market, prompting Honda to roll out the electrified two-door in Europe as well.
Honda isn't simply slapping a badge onto the trunk and calling it a day. The 2027 Limited Edition gets an exclusive Premium Crystal Garnet Metallic exterior color, a dark red shade that suits the coupe quite nicely, we’d add. Look closer, and you’ll also spot subtle red accents on the bumpers, complemented by Brembo brake calipers hiding behind the 19-inch black wheels.
The interior isn’t standard either, with the Prelude Limited Edition getting a burgundy theme (Bordeaux) for a considerably more upscale appearance than the regular car. To spruce things up, Honda adds new floor mats and red stitching to the steering wheel, center console, dashboard, front seats, and door panels.
2027 Honda Prelude Limited Edition (Europe)
As a final touch, the Prelude logo is embroidered into the dashboard, and Honda claims it’s meant to give each car the impression of being “hand-signed,” which is a fancy way of saying you’re getting a few extra red threads and a logo.
Production numbers weren't disclosed in the announcement, so it remains unclear how limited it really is. We do know it’ll be available in Europe this fall as a 2027 model year.
Pricing hasn’t been revealed either, but it certainly won’t be cheap, especially since Europeans pay value-added tax. For reference, a base Prelude is already €49,500 in Germany, where VAT is 19 percent, a far worse deal than in the United States, where Honda sells you one for $43,695.
2027 Honda Prelude Limited Edition (Europe)
Since the Limited Edition was born in Japan, it’s worth noting that this identical Prelude (well, with the steering wheel on the right side) costs 6,306,300 yen in its domestic market. That works out to about $40,000 or €35,300 at current exchange rates.
To be fair, some of that premium over a regular Civic goes toward hardware you don't get in the more mundane hybrid. The Prelude borrows goodies from the Type R, including adaptive dampers, wider front and rear tracks, and a dual-pinion electronic power steering (EPS) system. Additionally, the Brembo front brakes are larger than those on the run-of-the-mill Civic.
In other words, you're paying for more than just the swoopy profile and Prelude name.
The Honda S+ Shift technology debuted in the Prelude but has since trickled down to the regular Civic, where it also simulates an eight-speed automatic transmission, complete with downshift blips, rev matching, and gear holding.
That said, a Limited Edition like this would arguably make more sense as a hotter version of the car rather than primarily an appearance package. Unfortunately for anyone hoping for a more powerful Prelude, Honda has already ruled out a Type R or anything like that. At the other end of the lineup, the company has also dismissed the idea of introducing a cheaper entry-level trim. At the same time, a proper manual isn't happening either.
Of course, things could change in the long run, especially since the Prelude is still relatively new and has many years of shelf life ahead. For example, Honda Racing Corporation (HRC) has already shown us what an amped-up version will look like. Although it's technically a concept for now, these "Performance Parts" are actually going into production, so you'll be able to buy them one day.
Meanwhile, while this car's name may suggest something a little more special under the hood, this Limited Edition is mostly about making the Prelude look and feel more exclusive. It whets our appetite for something more substantial, ideally arriving later in the car's life cycle.
